purpose: Measure only the incremental owner-review burden of the richer J1 metadata that survived C4-C8.
owner_task: For each card, decide whether the extra information is a reasonable amount and type of information for you to review when making the governing decision. You are not being asked to understand internal schema, JSON, graph mechanics, or implementation details.

verdict_options.ACCEPTABLE: This is a reasonable amount/type of extra information to review with the governing decision.
verdict_options.NEEDS_SIMPLIFICATION: The underlying information is useful, but the owner-facing review should be simpler or smaller.
verdict_options.CANNOT_JUDGE: This still requires architecture/schema knowledge that should not be necessary.

burden_options.LOW: The extra review feels small and straightforward.
burden_options.MODERATE: It is noticeable additional review, but still practical for consequential governing decisions.
burden_options.HIGH: It is burdensome enough that this should not normally be required.

cards.previously_accepted_meaning: Deterministic consequential Project-system predicates/decisions must be defined executably and regression-tested.
extra_owner_visible_information: This is a tracked governing requirement with a stable identity.
It counts as complete only when an executable normative definition exists and the required regression verification passes.
The completion rule is set by the governing decision or an accepted verification contract, not by the implementer who claims the work is done.

cards.previously_accepted_meaning: A governing acceptance binds the human carrier, operative component and exact referenced domain-contract revisions as one accepted meaning boundary.
extra_owner_visible_information: This is a tracked governing requirement with a stable identity.
It counts as complete only when the required human carrier, operative component and referenced domain-contract revisions are all bound exactly and acceptance validation passes.
The requirement cannot silently disappear from tracking. It must remain open, become satisfied, be validly deferred, or later be changed/retired through a governed decision.

cards.previously_accepted_meaning: Research 438 prospectively amends Research 437 for the reconciled successor-design scope.
extra_owner_visible_information: The owner-facing lifecycle summary says which earlier governing meaning is being changed and which newer governing meaning replaces it for the stated scope.
Anything outside that stated scope is not silently changed by this decision.
If part of an older requirement has no successor, that loss/retirement must be shown explicitly rather than disappearing from the lineage.
